To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
male song and tegmina shape are both under significant multivariate sexual selection in wild sagebrush cricket populations, and that these traits are correlated in ways that may be adaptive.

male song is subject to significant linear (directional and stabilizing selection) and nonlinear (disruptive and correlational) sexual selection, and the structures that underlie male song are also subject to significant linear sexual selection, but not to significant nonlinear sexual selection.

the size and shape of the bottom tegmen were subject to strong directional and stabilizing sexual selection in wild populations of Cyphoderrus strepitans, while the size and shape (but not the symmetry) of the top tegmen were subject only to weak stabilizing sexual selection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of wing morphology in the sexual selection of song, and the role of song in the sexual selection on wing morphology.
the evolution of the male song in a species of crickets in which females feed on the male song organ.
how sexual selection on song is translated into selection on the morphometric traits that underlie song production in a wild population of crickets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the morphological structure that underlies the production and amplification of male song in sagebrush crickets is subject to strong sexual selection in natural populations, and that the strength of sexual selection on this morphological structure is not uniform across the entire structure, but rather is localized to specific regions.
sexual selection on male song is a complex process that is mediated by a number of morphological traits, including the size, shape and symmetry of the tegmina.
sexual selection on the morphology of the tegmina in wild sagebrush crickets is strong, complex and multifaceted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
male crickets are subject to strong sexual selection on their song structure, but the morphology of the structures that underlie this variation is also under intense selection.
sexual selection on the morphology underlying song structure is more complex than previously thought.

the male sagebrush cricket’s song is a product of both natural and sexual selection, and that sexual selection has had a greater impact on the morphology underlying song structure than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the song structures that underlie the variation in male song have evolved in concert with the morphological structures on which they are based, and that sexual selection on the latter may have played a significant role in the evolution of the former.

sexual selection on song structure is not necessarily a direct function of the strength of selection on song traits, but rather a consequence of the morphological structures involved in song production and the strength and form that selection acts on these structures.

the morphology of the tegmina is subject to intense multivariate sexual selection in this species, and the strength and form is not necessarily consistent with the strength and form documented on the song traits that the tegmina help to produce.
